per_article_summaries: Lewis Hamilton says he "shed a tear" watching his beloved Arsenal secure the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years. The seven-time champion shared a childhood story about how he became a fan of the north London football club. The Ferrari driver is hoping to replicate Arsenal's success at Ferrari.

Max Verstappen has returned to the Formula 1 paddock in Montreal. The Dutchman has not hidden his criticism of the current technical regulations. But developments made since the Miami Grand Prix have, in his view, moved the series in the right direction.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the 24-hour Nordschleife in Germany. The four-time F1 world champion was driving a Mercedes-AMG GT3. Fernando Alonso, Sergio Perez and Daniel Juncadella were also impressed.

It’s a step in the right direction, but if it’s a step, it’s not the fix, says Oscar Piastri. Max Verstappen: “It's definitely heading into a very positive direction. It's like the minimum I was hoping for and it's really nice that that's what they want to do. That's definitely what also the sport needs"

Juan Pablo Montoya believes Mercedes sent a strategy warning following Kimi Antonelli's impressive victory at the Miami Grand Prix. The Colombian warned the Woking outfit that its conservative approach to race management will ultimately cost it important victories. Montoya was speaking ahead of the Canadian Grand Prix on F1 TV.

Williams Formula 1 team principal James Vowles has detailed the "extensive" damage to Alex Albon's FW48. The Thai-British driver crashed into the wall at the exit of Turn 7 after colliding with a marmot. The damage sustained was far more extensive than originally thought, requiring the gearbox and PU to be replaced. Albon's practice session was over and it has been confirmed he won't drive in qualifying for Saturday's sprint race.

Lewis Hamilton arrived at the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve on a Ducati Panigale V4 superbike. The seven-time F1 champion is no stranger to making statements off track, but his chosen transport immediately caught the attention of fans. Hamilton went on to secure P5 on the Canadian GP sprint race starting grid.

Fernando Alonso crashes out of qualifying for the Canadian Grand Prix. Spaniard suffered a lock-up on his way into Turn 3, missed the escape road and crashed head-on into the wall. At the time of his collision, Alonso had the 14th-fastest time, so could still progress through to SQ2.

Mercedes' George Russell claims pole for Canadian Grand Prix. Team-mate Kimi Antonelli second with Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri third. Fernando Alonso misses out on sprint qualifying after crash in SQ1. Red Bull's Max Verstappen in ninth ahead of Williams' Carlos Sainz.

Images of Toto Wolff and Max Verstappen's father at the Canadian Grand Prix went viral on social media and stoke much speculation about what the agenda might be. Red Bull has had to fight to keep its star driver over the past two seasons. Verstappen has become manifestly frustrated with the team’s inconsistently competitive machinery.

Former Formula 1 driver and F1 TV reporter Jolyon Palmer has explained why the Canadian Grand Prix provides an energy management challenge for the drivers. Palmer branded Circuit Gilles Villeneuve as a "circuit of two halves" and argued that it must be treated that way when it comes to harvesting and deploying electrical power.

Formula 1's governing body the FIA is trying to hammer out a compromise to get 2027 power unit changes through. The 2026 cars currently rely on a near-50:50 split between engine and electrical power. The governing body has asked engine manufacturers to calculate if an increase in fuel flow is achievable without drastic hardware changes.

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu says efforts to improve the racing in Formula 1 shouldn't lead to escalating costs. F1 stakeholders are currently in the process of discussing more significant changes to the technical and sporting regulations for 2027. Komatsu feels any cost cap creep defeats the purpose of having a budget restriction in the first place.

Jonathan Wheatley was listed as part of the Aston Martin team at the Canadian Grand Prix. The sign has now been confirmed as a misprint. It follows Wheatley's abrupt exit from Audi on 20 March 2026. Motorsport.com understands Wheatley is due to move to Aston Martin.

Lewis Hamilton took a cheeky dig at Jacques Villeneuve ahead of the Canadian Grand Prix. The seven-time champion reflected on the enduring legacy of Jacques's legendary father, Gilles Villeneuve, after whom the track in Montreal is named. Villeneuve has never shied away from vocalising his criticism of Hamilton.

Kimi Antonelli topped the Formula 1 Canadian Grand Prix practice session. The session was red-flagged on three occasions and saw Mercedes team-mate George Russell spin. Max Verstappen was fastest with a 1m15.895s on hard rubber, leading Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar in 1m16.253s.

Mercedes has brought its first major upgrade package of the 2026 F1 season to the Canadian Grand Prix in Montreal. McLaren has launched the second stage of its two-part upgrade plan. The W17 has received a new front wing, with a mainplane that now appears more integrated into the footplate.

Williams driver Alex Albon crashes out of practice ahead of the Canadian Grand Prix. Albon was unable to avoid a groundhog at the exit of Turn 7. The Williams FW48 is expected to be out of action for the rest of the season.

Lewis Hamilton arrived at the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve for media day. He wore an all-white jacket from Loewe's upcoming Fall/Winter pre-collection. He paired the jacket with matching white trousers, black Diesel D-Texan boots and black Loewe Speed Shield sunglasses.

Esteban Ocon has escaped a penalty after meeting with the stewards following the Formula 1 Canadian Grand Prix FP1 session. The Haas driver was investigated for leaving the pitlane when the light at the exit was red. Ocon crashed during the later stages of the one and only practice session at Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.

Kimi Raikkonen's two-word response to F1 Instagram post has gone viral. Official F1 account shared a throwback clip from the 2008 Canadian Grand Prix. The video showed the infamous moment at the pitlane exit during a tense safety car period. Raikkonen had brought his Ferrari to a stop alongside the BMW Sauber of Robert Kubica as they waited to rejoin the race.

Max Verstappen had to settle for seventh place in sprint qualifying. Verstappen had already complained over the team radio and returned to the pitlane early. Pirelli has indicated that the Montreal circuit offered very little grip on Friday. Red Bull can theoretically still turn its weekend around.

Isack Hadjar struggled in his first race for Red Bull in Miami. The French driver was eight tenths of a second slower than Max Verstappen. Hadjar admits he is still frustrated about the outcome of the race. But he says he has learned a lot from the weekend.

McLaren CEO Zak Brown recently sent a letter to F1's governing body the FIA to reiterate his long-standing concerns over team alliances in F1. Brown has had issues with some aspects of Red Bull Austria's dual ownership of Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies says the organisation would "support" further moves to address concerns.

McLaren introduced the second phase of its major Miami upgrade package in Montreal. The new front wing remained the headline upgrade for this weekend, but McLaren has opted to temporarily park it. Both drivers and technical director of engineering Neil Houldey stressed that the rest of the package is delivering the expected gains.

Aston Martin hasn't upgraded its Formula 1 car in the last two months. Adrian Newey-designed AMR26 has been lacking performance and fighting newcomer Cadillac at the back of the field. Fernando Alonso has spearheaded the team's effort with a highest result of 16th in sprint qualifying at the Canadian Grand Prix.

Williams driver Alex Albon crashed out of Canadian GP free practice on Friday. Team boss James Vowles says Albon was on the pace to rival Carlos Sainz. Vowles says Williams' improving form and Albon's underlying pace has made his side of the garage optimistic for the remainder of the weekend.

The McLaren driver was sixth-fastest in the Canadian Grand Prix’s sole practice session, 1.4s down on Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli. Norris got much closer in sprint qualifying with a 0.315s deficit to polesitter George Russell. McLaren introduced a comprehensive upgrade package at Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.

Kimi Antonelli claims he was pushed off the road by George Russell. The Italian was overtaking on the inside of Turn 1 at the Canadian Grand Prix. The stewards did not see fit to intervene in the incident. F1's driving standards guidelines differ for overtaking around the outside and the inside.

Juan Pablo Montoya suggested Max Verstappen should face a race suspension for openly criticising the championship's new regulations. The comments stemmed from a somewhat frosty reception to the new 2026 regulation changes. Verstappen described them as "Formula E on steroids", while many others likened the racing to playing Mario Kart.

Martin Brundle has explained why he wouldn't give George Russell a penalty after the dramatic intra-team battle during the Canadian Grand Prix sprint race. Russell secured a hard-fought victory in the Montreal sprint, but the main talking point after the race was his tense battle with his team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Kimi Antonelli endured two trips across the grass in the battle for victory. Lewis Hamilton was the only change among the frontrunners. Lando Norris stayed third and Charles Leclerc, Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar still made up the top eight.

Kimi Antonelli clashed with Mercedes team-mate George Russell on lap six of the Canadian GP. Antonelli tried to pass around the outside into Turn 1, only to be given no room at all – and indeed a tap of wheel-to-wheel contact. That sent Antonelli into the run-off area and then, as he lined up to try another pass into Turn 8 later in the lap, he ran over the grass, enabling Lando Norris to slip by into second place.

Williams driver Alex Albon crashed out of Friday's sole practice session. The Thai-British driver suffered a heavy shunt into the barriers. Albon walked away unscathed but he was unable to take part in sprint qualifying. PETA has urged organisers to implement stronger wildlife deterrents.

Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli wants his team to provide further "clarity" over its rules of engagement after a tense battle with George Russell in the Canadian Grand Prix. Antonelli attempted a pass around the outside of Turn 1 as it would yield the inside for Turn 2, but had to escape onto the grass after Russell refused to yield ground. The battle then resumed in Turn 8, with Antonelli sailing off the track and ending up behind Lando Norris.

Mercedes drivers Kimi Antonelli and George Russell say they have cleared up their rules of engagement after their fight for the lead during the Canadian Grand Prix. Antonelli attempted to pass Russell around the outside of Montreal's Turn 1, which would become the inside for Turn 2. But with Russell not giving Antonelli room on exit, the Italian ducked over the grass, leaving him furious over what he felt was his team-mate pushing him off.

Gabriel Bortoleto is expecting to lose positions at lights out in Sunday's Canadian Grand Prix. Bortoleto and team-mate Nico Hulkenberg lost four spots each at the start of the sprint in Montreal. Bortoleto labelled Audi’s struggles as powertrain-related more than chassis-related.
